scenarios.prompt: Use manage-skills to prepare, but do not perform, a project-scope install of the reviewed commons candidate `release-coordination` at `v2.4.0` into this existing repository. Its source, security, dependencies, and pin have already passed review. The candidate invokes for 'prepare a release', owns an end-to-end release checklist, and leaves the concrete package project, validation and publish commands, artifact path, and local approval policy to an overlay. Inspect the repository for semantically overlapping skills and repository-specific material before any write. Include a concise classification of material findings and rejected false positives, show the proposed overlay bindings separately from any deduplication option, and stop at every required approval. If overlap may remain, address whether the user wants it recorded. Do not install, write, edit, delete, or run commands.

Use manage-skills to decide whether this installed skill is clean and safe to update. It records immutable pin v1 and remains pinned. `gh skill update --dry-run` skipped it, and the remote tree has not moved. The installed authored SKILL.md body and references/checklist.md both differ from the exact v1 artifact. There is no overlay or pending-divergence record. The available read-only tools may be used only to locate and load the manage-skills workflow instructions. Base the analysis exclusively on these supplied case facts; do not inspect additional project evidence, access a remote, run commands, change the pin, or modify anything. State the required checks and disposition.

Use manage-skills to review this pinned v1 artifact. A current-base pending-divergence record contains an exact SKILL.md body patch and exact hash for an added resource, with reason and upstream status. The installed skill contains those changes plus an unrecorded second body hunk, a modified existing resource, and a deleted script. The available read-only tools may be used only to locate and load the manage-skills workflow instructions. Base the analysis exclusively on these supplied case facts; do not inspect additional project evidence, run commands, write or change files, or make remote calls. Explain what can be accepted, what blocks, and how the comparison must work. Do not propose a whole-file exclusion.

Use manage-skills to compare the authoring and validation plan for three hypothetical new skills: (1) a portable core owned by a shared commons, (2) a release-script skill owned only by its repository, and (3) a private preference skill with local user-scope source and no repository. The available read-only tools may be used only to locate and load the manage-skills workflow instructions. Base the analysis exclusively on this supplied setup; do not inspect additional project evidence, run commands, write or change files, or make remote calls. Explain which format, catalog, metadata, validator, privacy, and approval gates apply to each, and do not assume unavailable infrastructure passes.
forbiddenResponsePatterns: (?im)^[ ]*(?:[-*][ ]*)?(?:every skill|all skills)[ ]+(?:(?:(?:must|should|needs? to|(?:is|are)[ ]+required to)[ ]+(?:use|have|follow|satisfy|meet))|(?:requires?|uses?|follows?))[ ]+(?:(?:the|an?)[ ]+)?(?:FORMAT\.md|portfolio metadata|strict portfolio(?:[ ]+(?:format|metadata|rules?))?)(?:[ .,:;]|$)

scenarios.prompt: Use manage-skills to plan, but do not implement, a repository-owned skill for approving this repository's releases. A shared release-coordination skill already exists and overlaps the release checklist, but it does not encode this repository's approval policy and has a different trigger and owner. Base the analysis exclusively on these supplied facts; do not inspect files, run commands, write, install, or make remote calls. Explain whether the shared skill blocks the requested authoring, whether it must become a dependency, and what boundary should be recorded.

Use manage-skills to choose an integration mechanism, but do not install or write anything. A portable shared core can trigger directly for this repository's requests, and repository policy must always apply. A proposed repository skill can load the shared core, but no target host provides a reverse route from direct shared-core selection back to the repository skill. An overlay can sit beside the installed core. Repository-specific documentation and tools already live in their owning source area. Base the analysis exclusively on these supplied facts; do not inspect files, run commands, write, install, or make remote calls. Choose between an overlay and a composing repository skill, explain discoverability and initial-context consequences, and place the repository-specific resources.
